transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-02
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (Helix - Procurement), Evan Chu (Helix - Legal), Arjun Patel (Helix - InfoSec), Samir Khan (Helix - CTO)

[00:00] Liam Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Liam, AE at Redwood. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer. We're here to walk through the MSA/DPA and the SLA asks and make sure onboarding plan is clear.

[00:25] Marta Lopez: Hi Liam, Priya. Thanks. We just want to make sure timelines and the legal language line up with our procurement windows. Evan and Arjun are on for the legal and security concerns.

[00:40] Evan Chu: Hi, yes. We got the initial MSA and DPA last week. Quick heads up — we have a few asks around the SLA uptime, breach notification timelines, and some indemnity language.

[01:10] Priya Desai: Totally, thanks for flagging. To set expectations — Redwood's standard SLA is 99.9% for hosted API with credits for downtime. For Dedicated we can talk about higher SLOs and custom commits. Happy to go through the sections you'd like to redline.

[01:40] Arjun Patel: On security, we need clarity on encryption at rest and in transit, KMS/HSM integrations, audit log retention (we typically require 7 years for certain events), and whether private deployment is an option for regulated workloads.

[02:10] Samir Khan: And on the procurement side we need approved pricing bands and how burst capacity is billed. We have a Q4 initiative to pilot inference across two teams, so timeline is tight.

[02:45] Liam Carter: Understood. Quick overview: pricing model options are usage-based for hosted, reserved capacity for Dedicated (monthly/annual commits), and an enterprise Private deployment option for regulated workloads. For pilot we typically recommend a short reserved Dedicated pool or hosted with burst — we'll share a cost projection.

[03:20] Marta Lopez: For the MSA, Evan is concerned about the SLA remedy wording — credits vs monetary penalties and the exact measurement window.

[03:45] Evan Chu: Right. The current clause references service credits but doesn't specify how uptime is calculated during incidents with partial regional impact. Also we'd like to see maximum liability caps tied to a longer period than 12 months.

[04:15] Priya Desai: Noted. For uptime calc we use per-region availability and per-route metrics; Priya tries to explain: it's a rolling 30-day window for hosted. For Dedicated we can set monthly review and a 99.95% target if committed capacity is purchased.

[04:50] Liam Carter: We can expand the SLA exhibit to include regional granularity and specific measurement methodology. We're flexible on credits, and for enterprise customers we can negotiate higher uptime and different remedies.

[05:20] Arjun Patel: About data — we need confirmation that customer data used for inference is not used to train Redwood models and that logs are segregated. Also want details on where logs are stored and retention controls.

[05:50] Priya Desai: Standard Redwood policy: we do not train models on customer request data by default; there is an explicit opt-in program for training. We'll put that in the DPA. Logs are stored in encrypted buckets; for Private deployments that's subject to customer-managed storage/KMS. We'll share the audit log schema and retention options.

[06:25] Samir Khan: Can you also confirm support SLAs during the pilot — response times for Sev1/Sev2, and escalation path?

[06:45] Liam Carter: Yes — our standard support tiers: 1 hour initial response for Sev1 on enterprise plan, 4 hours for Sev2, with a named CSM for dedicated contracts. We'll include escalation matrix in the onboarding packet.

[07:10] Marta Lopez: On procurement timeline — we need final legal approval by Nov 15 to hit our internal procurement cycle. Is that feasible?

[07:30] Evan Chu: Assuming Redwood sends updated MSA with requested language by next week, we can review and return redlines within 7 business days.

[07:50] Priya Desai: We'll aim to send the redlined MSA and an SLA exhibit by 2027-11-05. We'll also attach a dedicated onboarding runbook and perf benchmark spreadsheet we ran for similar finance customers.

[08:20] Liam Carter: On pricing — for the pilot we can propose a 3-month reserved Dedicated commit at a modest level to guarantee throughput, with ability to scale. Or hosted usage-based with a committed spend cap to control costs. We'll follow up with a pricing spreadsheet.

[09:00] Samir Khan: If we do dedicated commit, what are the minimum terms and how flexible is scaling/cancellation?

[09:20] Priya Desai: Typical minimum is one month for pilot commits, with a 30-day notice for downsizing after the initial period. For annual committed capacity there are discounts. We'll include the cancellation/termination language in the doc.

[09:50] Evan Chu: Also, regarding DPA — we need explicit breach notification timelines (72 hours preferred), subprocessors list, and the right to audit. The DPA we received had some of that but we want clarity on audit scope and frequency.

[10:15] Liam Carter: We can confirm 72-hour notification and a subprocessor list; audit rights are typically mediated — for hosted we provide SOC2 reports and support audits through third-party attestations. For Private deployments customers can run on-prem audits. We'll add language to describe both paths.

[10:50] Arjun Patel: On KMS — we want customer-managed keys for encryption at rest for production workloads. Is that supported?

[11:05] Priya Desai: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we support customer KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM for higher assurance. For hosted we offer BYOK for certain enterprise customers; we'll confirm the exact supported configurations.

[11:35] Marta Lopez: There was also a question from procurement about indemnity and export compliance clauses — we need those aligned with our corporate policies.

[11:50] Evan Chu: Export compliance is material for us. Also please flag any third-party open-source model licensing obligations if Redwood supplies model binaries.

[12:15] Priya Desai: Good point — if we provide model binaries, we'll include license disclosures. In many cases we route customers to validated open models; we'll enumerate any licensing constraints in the onboarding packet.

[12:40] Liam Carter: To keep us moving — we'll produce three artifacts: an updated MSA/DPA with redlines, an SLA exhibit detailing measurement and remedies, and a technical onboarding packet (benchmarks, KMS integrations, runbook). We'll share links in the follow-up email.

[13:05] Samir Khan: Are there any competitors in your legal terms? We need to understand differences vs. MegaCloud AI and Atlas Inference — specifically uptime commitments and pricing flexibility.

[13:25] Liam Carter: We're competitive on latency and cost, and we emphasize production-grade SLOs plus private deployment options. We'll add a short comparison doc; but legal terms do vary — we'll highlight the SLA and audit pathways.

[13:45] Marta Lopez: Operational question — onboarding timeline: once MSA signed how quickly can you get a pilot running?

[14:00] Priya Desai: Typical pilot setup is 1-2 weeks for hosted with test dataset and endpoints; Dedicated can be stood up within 2-3 weeks depending on capacity provisioning. Private deployments take longer — usually 4-6 weeks.

[14:30] Evan Chu: On audit retention — you mentioned audit log schema. We need to confirm what events are captured and the ability to export logs to our SIEM.

[14:50] Priya Desai: The schema includes request/response IDs, tokens generated, caller identity, and model route. We can stream logs to customer S3 or SIEM via secure forwarders; retention configurable per contract. We'll share sample schema.

[15:20] Arjun Patel: Any PII redaction or masking options for logs?

[15:35] Priya Desai: We support configurable masking at ingestion and prefix KV caching controls; for finance workloads we typically recommend prefix hashing and masked logs. We'll include recommended configs in the runbook.

[16:00] Liam Carter: Let's talk specifics on SLA numbers for the MSA redline. Marta, what would be acceptable uptime and remedies for you to get procurement approval?

[16:20] Marta Lopez: For production pilot we'd like 99.95% for Dedicated with credits and an option for higher uptime in exchange for financial commitment. For hosted, 99.9% is acceptable if credits are meaningful.

[16:40] Evan Chu: We still need caps on liability; we prefer liability cap at greater of fees paid in prior 12 months or a fixed amount. Currently the MSA has a 12-month lookback; we'd prefer 24 months or a fixed threshold.

[17:05] Liam Carter: We'll propose language that ties cap to fees paid in the previous 24 months or a fixed floor — open to negotiation. We'll surface that in the updated doc.

[17:30] Samir Khan: Do you have a reference customer in finance we can speak to about production behavior and latency?

[17:45] Priya Desai: Yes — we can share an anonymized case study and connect you to a peer reference under NDA. We'll include that in the follow-up.

[18:10] Marta Lopez: Ok good. On the pricing spreadsheet — can you provide both hosted and Dedicated cost projections for a pilot that expects 500k tokens/day?

[18:30] Liam Carter: Absolutely — we'll provide cost scenarios for hosted with usage cap and a 3-month Dedicated commit with projected savings.

[18:50] Evan Chu: One more legal nit — indemnity for IP claims related to model outputs. We need clarity who bears liability if model output causes downstream harm.

[19:10] Priya Desai: We typically limit liability for model-generated outputs; however for enterprise customers with specific requirements we can carve out additional protections or indemnities — but that might come with different pricing and review. We'll flag that for legal.

[19:40] Arjun Patel: Anything about data residency? For EU customer data we require EU region storage. Is regional pinning possible?

[19:55] Liam Carter: Yes — we can pin region for data residency on hosted or use Dedicated/Private in region. We'll note region pinning options in the SLA exhibit.

[20:20] Marta Lopez: Great. Let's confirm timeline again: Redwood will send updated MSA/DPA and SLA exhibit by Nov 5; Helix legal will reply with redlines by Nov 12; goal to sign by Nov 15.

[20:40] Liam Carter: That's our target. We'll also include the perf benchmarks, onboarding runbook, and pricing spreadsheet in the same email.

[21:05] Priya Desai: Quick tech note: for benchmarking we used a mix of small- and large-context prompts; we'll include p99 latency and cost per 1k tokens for the models we recommend.

[21:30] Samir Khan: Perfect. Any blockers from Redwood's side for the pilot start date if MSA is signed on Nov 15?

[21:50] Liam Carter: None — we can start provisioning immediately. We'll need accounts for your engineers and a short tech kickoff meeting to walk the runbook.

[22:10] Marta Lopez: Sounds good. Evan, Arjun anything else?

[22:20] Evan Chu: No, looks like the main items are MSA SLA language, DPA breach timelines, and audit scope. We'll review the redline next week.

[22:35] Arjun Patel: I'll prepare KMS requirements and SIEM integration spec and send by Nov 10.

[22:50] Liam Carter: Great. We'll summarize next steps now.

[23:05] Liam Carter: Recap: Redwood to send updated MSA/DPA and SLA exhibit + perf benchmarks + onboarding runbook by 2027-11-05. Helix to return legal redlines by 2027-11-12. Pilot kickoff post-signature targeted following week. Action items captured.

[23:40] Marta Lopez: Thanks everyone. We'll watch for the email and set up a legal review slot next week.

[23:55] Samir Khan: Thanks, talk soon.

[24:05] Liam Carter: Thanks all, bye.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional transcription errors and shorthand; refer to attached artifacts for canonical wording (MSA_v3.pdf, DPA_v2.pdf, SLA_exhibit.xlsx, onboarding_runbook_link).
